summary: Fixed the --lit consumer-side silent-failure anti-pattern across all six core skills (skill-researcher, skill-planner, skill-implementer, and their -hard variants). Previously each of the 18 Stage 4a invocation sites (3 per skill) ran `lit_context=$(bash .claude/scripts/literature-briefing.sh 2>/dev/null) || lit_context=""`, discarding stderr and collapsing a script crash into the same empty value a legitimately-empty briefing produces, violating CLAUDE.md's '--lit is never a silent no-op' contract. Created a new shared wrapper, .claude/scripts/literature-briefing-invoke.sh, that passes args through to literature-briefing.sh unchanged, lets stderr flow, and on non-zero exit emits a visible '[lit] briefing generation failed (exit N)' notice to stderr while still exiting 0 to preserve callers' fallback semantics. Repointed all 18 sites at the wrapper with 2>/dev/null removed, and rewrote the stale '# - script exited with error' trailing comment in the live bash block of each skill (skill-implementer-hard had no such comment block to rewrite, correctly left as-is). Verified: zero residual literature-briefing.sh 2>/dev/null occurrences, exactly 3 literature-briefing-invoke.sh references per skill, literature-briefing.sh / literature-lit-flag-resolve.sh / the four skill-cslib-* skills all byte-unchanged, wrapper syntax-clean and executable, and both success-path (stdout byte-identical to direct invocation) and failure-path (single stderr notice, empty stdout, wrapper exit 0) manually verified.
